# Bonusly, the platform for employee recognition, raises $9 million Series A \| TechCrunch

Bonusly, a platform that involves the entire organization in recognizing employees and rewarding them, closed on a $9 million Series A financing round led by Access Venture Partners\. Next Frontier Capital, Operator Partners and existing investor FirstMark Capital also participated in the round\.

Bonusly launched in 2013 when co-founder and CEO Raphael Crawford-Marks saw the opportunity to reinvent the way employers and colleagues recognize and reward their employees/coworkers\.

“I knew that, in order to be successful, companies would be shifting their approach to employee experience and I thought software could enable that shift,” said Crawford-Marks\. “Bonusly was this elegant idea of empowering employees to give each other timely, frequent and meaningful recognition that would not only benefit employees because they would feel recognized but also surface previously hidden information to the entire company about who was working with whom and on what and what strengths they were bringing to the workplace\.”

Most employers use year-end bonuses and performance reviews to motivate workers, with some employers providing some physical rewards\.

Bonusly thinks recognition should happen year-round\. The platform works with the employers on their overall budget for recognition and rewards, and breaks that down into “points” that are allotted to all employees at the organization\.

These employees can give out points to other co-workers, whether they’re direct reports or managers or peers, at any time throughout the year\. Those points translate to a monetary value that can be redeemed by the employee at any time, whether it’s through PayPal as a cash reward or with one of Bonusly’s vendor partners, including Amazon, Tango Card and Cadooz\. Bonusly also partners with nonprofit organizations to let employees redeem their points via charitable donation\.

In fact, Crawford-Marks noted that Bonusly users just crossed the $500,000 mark for total donations, and have donated more than $100,000 to the WHO in six weeks\.

Techcrunch event

San Francisco \| October 13-15, 2026

Bonusly integrates with several collaboration platforms, including Gmail and Slack, to give users the flexibility to give points in whatever venue they choose\. Bonusly also has a feed, not unlike social media sites like Twitter, that shows in real time employees who have received recognition\.

The company has also built in some technical features to help with usability\. For example, Bonusly understands the social organization of a company, surfacing the most relevant folks in the point feed based on who employees have given or received points to/from in the past\. In a company with tens of thousands of employees, this keeps Bonusly relevant\.

Bonusly has also incorporated tools for employers, including an auto-scale button for employers with workers in multiple jurisdictions or companies\. The button allows employers to scale up or down the point allotments in different geographies based on cost of living\.

There are also privacy controls on Bonusly that allow high-level employees and leadership to give each other recognition for projects that may not be widely known about at the company yet, like say for an acquisition that was completed\.

Bonusly says that peer-to-peer recognition is more powerful than manager-only recognition, saying it’s nearly 36% more likely to have better financial outcomes\.

The company also cites research that says that a happy workforce raises business productivity by more than 30%\.

Bonusly competes with Kazoo and Motivocity, and Crawford-Marks says that the biggest differentiation factor is participation\.

“We set a very high bar for how we measure participation and engagement in the platform,” he said\. “You’ll see other companies claiming really high participation rates, but typically if you dig into that they’re talking about getting recognition every six months or every year or just logging in, rather than giving recognition every single month, month over month\.”

He noted that 75% of employees on average give recognition in the first month of deployment with an organization, and that number gradually increases over time\. By the two-year mark, 80% of employees are giving recognition every month\.

Bonusly has raised a total of nearly $14 million in funding since inception\.

Jordan Crook was the Deputy Editor of TechCrunch\.

, /PRNewswire/ -- Bonusly, the leading employee recognition platform, announced the launch of new video capabilities that revolutionize how employee recognition is given and received\. With these new features, organizations can now add a personal, human touch to how teams connect, recognize, and grow together—no matter where or how they work\.

Built directly into the Bonusly platform, the new video features allow users to share recognition, celebrate milestones and wins, and engage in workplace culture in a more heartfelt, face-to-face way\. Whether it's a peer shoutout, a manager highlight, or a message from leadership, video brings a new level of authenticity, making recognition more meaningful and effective for every generation in the workforce\.

\"As work becomes more digital and distributed, the need for human connection is more important than ever,\" said Charles Hough, CEO of Bonusly\. \"We designed our new video functionality to help people show up more authentically and make recognition feel as personal as the impact behind it\.\"

With the new video feature, employees can now share recognition in Bonusly's social feed, blending written and video messages to create more meaningful, authentic interactions\. Recording directly in the platform makes it easy to recognize peers and celebrate achievements from anywhere\.

Modern recognition features like video are part of Bonusly's continued investment in helping organizations get recognition right—not as an afterthought, but as a fun way that every employee, in every work context, can play a part of\.

Recognition should do more than reward good work—it should fuel it\. Bonusly makes recognition meaningful, habitual, and connected to what matters most—helping organizations build engaged cultures where people want to stay and grow together\. More than 3,400 global organizations, including DoorDash, Toast, Seat Geek, and Magna-Tiles, use Bonusly to see what recognition done right can achieve\.

- **Boost employee engagement with an intuitive, and accessible interface\.** Developed from feedback and analytics from over 3,200 companies and 400,000 daily users, the new interface is functional and fun, with key platform data easy to find and act on and a WCAG AA accessibility supported interface\.

\"Research shows that employees who are appreciated are more loyal to their employers,\" said Luis Jiminez, People Experience Associate, Headspace\. \"And one of the many ways we appreciate employees for their wins, hard work, and success is through Bonusly\! Bonusly's employee recognition platform has made an impact on retention and has helped ensure our employees feel seen and recognized by not only their team but the entire company\.\"

Thousands of companies worldwide rely on Bonusly to build a winning culture of appreciation, and cultivate high-performing teams regardless of their location, work setting, or industry\. Bonusly serves as a crucial tool for investing in, and driving positive business outcomes from a company's most critical asset — their people\.

Bonusly's engagement software is easy to use and enables companies to build stronger connections among and between teams, leading to increased collaboration and innovation among your workforce\. Additionally, Bonusly provides exclusive insights at the individual, team, and company levels, empowering managers to make informed decisions regarding culture, professional growth, performance management, and employee retention\. # AftermathFi's Perpetuals V2 launches on mainnet after 12-week security review clears all major issues

AftermathFi is bringing its Perpetuals V2 to mainnet on August 18, and for once, the security story behind a DeFi launch is actually worth reading\. Blockchain security firm OtterSec spent 12 weeks combing through nine separate repositories of the protocol’s smart contracts and came up empty on critical and high-severity issues, a result that matters considerably more given what happened the last time AftermathFi ran a perpetuals product in production\.

The Sui-based decentralized exchange announced the audit completion on August 14, leaving a narrow four-day window before the live launch\.

## What the audit actually covered

Twelve weeks is a long runway for a smart contract review\. OtterSec is not a new name in this space\. The firm has a track record of securing protocols with over $36B in total value locked and has patched vulnerabilities cumulatively exceeding $1B across its client base\. It had previously reviewed components of AftermathFi’s infrastructure, including the Perps Oracle, in late 2025, so the team was not coming in cold\.

## The shadow of the April exploit

On April 29, 2026, AftermathFi suffered an exploit that drained approximately $1\.14M USDC from its original Perpetuals module\. The mechanism was a negative integrator fee validation flaw, a bug that let attackers inflate collateral balances and then withdraw funds that were not legitimately theirs\. The team paused all operations and began an investigation\.

That incident is the direct reason Perpetuals V2 exists\. The protocol did not patch and resume; it rebuilt, subjected the new architecture to a substantially longer and broader audit than is typical, and is now launching with a clean bill of health from an established security firm\.

## What this means for AftermathFi and the Sui ecosystem

OtterSec’s continued involvement with AftermathFi infrastructure, stretching back to the Perps Oracle review in late 2025, adds a layer of institutional continuity to the security narrative\. The four days between the audit announcement and the mainnet date give the market very little time to react before the product is live\.

# GameStop’s Zelda Ocarina of Time Pre-Order “Leak” Looks Like an Error

Share this article

Nintendo has confirmed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 in 2026, but it has not announced an official release date or pre-order schedule\. \(Nintendo\)

**Nintendo** officially announced **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time** for **Switch 2** in June, but it has not yet revealed the game’s release date, price, or pre-order schedule\. That lack of information recently turned what appears to be a retailer error into a widely shared Zelda “leak\.”

A GameStop search result reportedly displayed an August 4, 2026 date alongside the upcoming Ocarina of Time release\. Some fans interpreted the date as the start of pre-orders or even a possible launch date\.

However, the available evidence suggests that the date probably did not belong to Zelda at all\.

## The August 4 Date Likely Came From Another Game

August 4, 2026 is the confirmed release date for Beast of Reincarnation, an upcoming action RPG from Game Freak\. GameStop already has active product pages and pre-order information for the game\.

This makes a retailer database or search indexing error the most plausible explanation\. GameStop or Google may have pulled the August 4 date from Beast of Reincarnation and temporarily attached it to the Ocarina of Time search result\.

GameStop subsequently removed the date, and Nintendo has not made any related announcement\.

The incident therefore should not be treated as confirmation that Ocarina of Time pre-orders will begin on August 4\. It also does not reliably indicate when Nintendo will hold its next presentation\.

Retailer listings sometimes reveal games, editions, or release dates before publishers announce them\. However, they can also contain placeholders, copied product data, and incorrectly matched information\. In this case, the connection to another confirmed August 4 release makes the error explanation particularly convincing\.

**Newly released game**: Palworld 1\.0 Patch Notes: 72 New Pals, World Tree, Sunreach and Major Changes

## Nintendo Has Only Confirmed a 2026 Release

Nintendo officially revealed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time during its June 9 Nintendo Direct\. The company said the Nintendo 64 classic would return for a new generation exclusively on Switch 2 in 2026\.

The brief announcement trailer introduced the project but did not show extended gameplay\. Nintendo also withheld the exact release date, price, editions, and pre-order details\.

The company’s official store page still lists only “Coming 2026\.” It does not currently offer a purchase or pre-order button\.

Nintendo has also avoided explaining the full scope of the project\. The announcement describes Ocarina of Time as “reborn,” but we still do not know how closely it will follow the original game or the enhanced Nintendo 3DS version\.

More information should arrive before launch, particularly details about its updated visuals, controls, gameplay revisions, and technical performance on Switch 2\.

**See also**: Bethesda Finally Reveals What Comes Next for Fallout and The Elder Scrolls VI

## Play-Asia Lists the Game for $59\.99

Although GameStop does not currently accept Ocarina of Time pre-orders, Play-Asia has published product pages for several regional physical editions\.

The retailer lists the game for $59\.99 and marks its expected shipping date as TBA\. Customers can currently add the product to their carts, but Nintendo has not confirmed the price\.

The $59\.99 figure could represent genuine distributor information\. It could also be an estimated or placeholder price that Play-Asia will update later\.

Buyers should therefore avoid treating it as Nintendo’s official US launch price\. Nintendo could use different pricing across physical and digital editions, regions, or special packages\.

The listing does at least support the expectation that Ocarina of Time will receive a physical Switch 2 release\. However, final availability, packaging, and regional language support could change before launch\.

**Related news**: Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake Listed at $59\.99 Ahead of Nintendo Price Confirmation

## When Will Official Pre-Orders Begin?

Nintendo has not announced when pre-orders will open\. Any specific date remains speculation until Nintendo or an authorized retailer publishes confirmed purchase information\.

A new Nintendo Direct or dedicated Zelda presentation would be the most likely place for the company to reveal gameplay, editions, pricing, and a firm release date\. Retail pre-orders could open shortly after that announcement\.

For now, fans should treat the August 4 GameStop date as an apparent listing error rather than a reliable leak\.

The remake itself is official, and Nintendo still plans to release it for Switch 2 in 2026\. The rumored pre-order date is not\.

# Space NK beauty advent calendar 2026: All the latest news, price and launch updates

The Space NK beauty advent calendar 2026 is officially on the way, with the retailer becoming one of the latest to confirm its festive countdown and open waitlist sign-ups ahead of launch\. It joins Harrods, Cult Beauty and Sephora among the best beauty advent calendars announced so far, with retailers revealing their offerings earlier than they did in 2025, when launches largely began at the end of August and start of September\.

While Space NK is keeping most details under wraps for now, its brand manager Abbey Parkinson has teased “iconic hero products \[and\] exciting discovery brands,” giving beauty obsessives plenty to look forward to when the contents are unveiled later this month\. Particularly given the highly-coveted roster of products Space NK’s previous calendars \(think: K18, Refy and Westman Atelier\) have carried\.

I'll be updating this guide as more information is announced, including the contents list \(coming 19 August\), the official on-sale date and everything else you’ll need to know before it goes live\. Scroll on for all the early details, from pricing to packaging\.

**Read more: ****Everything we know so far about Cult Beauty’s 2026 advent calendar**

### Space NK beauty advent calendar 2026

At £275, the Space NK beauty advent calendar is £15 more expensive than last year's edition, but the retailer says its contents will be worth more than £1,200 \(£50 extra than 2025’s\), which still leaves you with an extra £35 of savings up for grabs\. With the full line-up still hush hush until 19 August, it's too early to say whether this price and worth increase will definitely result in a higher value product\. But I’m expecting more premium brands, additional full-size products and perhaps some bigger-ticket beauty buys\.

So far, Space NK has only teased a mix of \"iconic hero products\" and \"exciting discovery brands\.\" Looking at its recent brand onboardings, it’d be great to see the likes of Prequel and Takami featuring alongside established beauty favourites – and in-keeping with Parkinson’s ‘discovery brand’ suggestion\.

The calendar itself has been given a festive makeover, with pastel pink and blue nutcracker-splashed packaging that's – according to Space NK – also more environmentally conscious\. It's made from 100 per cent recyclable FSC-certified paper, printed using vegetable-based inks and designed to be reused or recycled after Christmas\.

Whether you’re waiting for the full list of contents or dead set on securing the Space NK advent this December, you’ll want to join the waitlist sooner rather than later\. Rather than giving everyone access at once, Space NK has declared that “the sooner you join, the earlier you can shop on preview day,” which implies that links to the live calendar will be sent based on when signees joined the waitlist\. So, an earlier place in the queue could improve your chances of getting hold of one before it sells out\. And, in my experience, it definitely will sell out\.

#### What to know

- **Price:** £275 \(up £15 year on year\)
- **Worth:** £1,200\+ \(up £50 year on year\)
- **Number of days:** 25
- **Number of products:** Not yet revealed
- **Advent calendar highlights:** Products announced 7am, 19 August – \"iconic hero products with exciting discovery brands\" promised
- **Available:** Not yet announced, waitlist open now

# An exclusive sneak peak at the Lookfantastic beauty advent calendar 2026

The Lookfantastic beauty advent calendar 2026 has been revealed exclusively to *The Independent*, with the retailer sharing the first details of its festive offering ahead of launch\. It joins the best beauty advent calendars announced so far, as brands including Harrods, Cult Beauty, Space NK, Sephora, Liberty and Harvey Nichols bring their Christmas countdowns to shoppers earlier than they did in 2025 – when most major launches landed from late August onwards\.

While some details are still to be confirmed, Lookfantastic has revealed that, for the first time ever, its advent offering will showcase an expert-selected product collection, with each of the 27 items hand-selected by beauty insiders \(including big-name influencers\), well-known experts and Lookfantastic’s own buying aficionados\. The retailer is known for its wide-ranging beauty edit, and its advent calendar usually follows suit, combining skincare, make-up, haircare and wellness brands in one collection that’s worth several times – more than five, to be exact – the value of what you pay upfront\.

This year will also see the return of Lookfantastic’s fragrance and grooming calendars, both of which sold out in 2025\. I'll be updating this guide as more information is announced, including the full contents, launch date and everything else you need to know before it goes on sale\. I'll also be getting hands-on with the calendar and testing the products inside as soon as I can, so stay tuned for my full review and verdict on whether it's *actually* worth adding to your pre-Christmas wishlist\.

**Read more: ****John Lewis 2026 beauty advent calendar pre-orders are live – here’s what’s included**

### Lookfantastic beauty advent calendar 2026

The biggest change for 2026 is the way Lookfantastic has approached curation\. Rather than a traditional edit chosen behind the scenes, each of the 25 doors has been hand-picked by a different beauty insider, expert or member of the retailer’s own team\. *The Independent* can reveal that this line-up includes *The Girls Bathroom* hosts Sophia Tuxford and Cinzia Baylis-Zullo, celebrity hairstylist Sam McKnight and social media star Gary Thompson\.

One of the Lookfantastic calendar’s biggest strengths has always been its price point\. While many of this calibre now cost somewhere between £200 and £300 \(with this number rising year-on-year\.\.\.\), the Lookfantastic calendar remains significantly more affordable without compromising on the breadth of brands or the overall value on offer\. Last year's calendar cost £105, was worth £655 and included 15 full-size products from brands including Elemis, Medik8, The White Company and Mac\. This year, the price has increased to £120, but so has the contents value to £665 and the number of full-size products to 19 – a promising sign that beauty addicts could be getting even more for their money in 2026\.

Lookfantastic has kept the contents under wraps \(for now\), with a few items obscured within metallic packaging\.\.\.but I think I’ve spotted a Sol de Janeiro bottle \(a brand that featured in 2025\) and possibly a Laneige lip sleeping mask tub among the props\. Of course, these items could be just that: props for shooting\. Nonetheless, I’ll be keeping a close eye as the brand begins to reveal the calendar’s confirmed product line-up from 17 August\. Stay tuned for the unveiling\.

If you're hoping to secure one \(or you’re not sure just yet\) I’d recommend joining the waitlist, regardless\. The calendar officially launches on 1 September\.

#### What to know

- **Worth:** £665
- **Number of days:** 25
- **Number of products:** 27 \(19 full-sizes\)
- **Advent calendar highlights:** Not confirmed, products being announced from 17 August onwards
- **Available:** 1 September, waitlist open now

Lookfantastic's fragrance advent calendar is also returning for 2026 after selling out in record time last year\. More details are due to be announced in the coming weeks, but if the 2025 edition is anything to go by, I'll be expecting another mix of premium perfumes, home fragrance and scented body care\. Last year's calendar featured brands including Floral Street, Neom, Marc Jacobs and Jo Malone, giving olfactory obsessives the chance to discover new scents and indulge in long-time fragrance favourites\. Once again, products will begin to be revealed from 17 August, ahead of the full launch on 1 September\.

The Lookfantastic fragrance advent calendar cost £130 in 2025 \(Lookfantastic/The Independent\)

Likewise, Lookfantastic’s grooming advent calendar is also back for 2026, bringing together another edit focused on skincare, haircare and everyday male grooming\. You guessed it, we'll have to wait a little longer for the full list of products, but previous grooming editions have included everything from shaving essentials and moisturisers to beard care and hair styling favourites\. I'll update this guide as each reveal lands and, as with the beauty calendar, our team will be taking a closer hands-on look once as soon as we can\.

The grooming advent variety cost £85 last year \(Lookfantastic/The Independent\)

This year, the price has increased to £120, but so has the contents value to £665 and the number of full-size products to 19 – a promising sign that beauty addicts could be getting even more for their money in 2026\.

Lookfantastic has kept the contents under wraps \(for now\), with a few items obscured within metallic packaging\.\.\.but I think I’ve spotted a Sol de Janeiro bottle \(a brand that featured in 2025\) and possibly a Laneige lip sleeping mask tub among the props\. Of course, these items could be just that: props for shooting\. Nonetheless, I’ll be keeping a close eye as the brand begins to reveal the calendar’s confirmed product line-up from 17 August\. Stay tuned for the unveiling\.

If you're hoping to secure one \(or you’re not sure just yet\) I’d recommend joining the waitlist, regardless\. The calendar officially launches on 1 September\.
